A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Sparse Attention Vectors study, with complete main text, references and Appendices A-D. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, tables, figures and qualitative examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of SAVs on LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Qwen2-VL-7B, including benchmark results, ablations, robustness analyses and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, language-only and online-learning results, and qualitative cases reported in v1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains final-token attention-vector extraction, class-centroid-based head selection and majority-vote classification. The appendix's randomized weighted-majority variant is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MHaluBench, VLGuard, BLINK, NaturalBench, EuroSAT, Oxford-IIIT-Pets, SST-2 and MNLI. The same subtasks, transfer settings and supplementary test scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: CLIP/SigLIP, zero-shot LMMs, MTV, last-layer/all-layer features and LoRA, alongside the retained KNN, linear-probe and few-shot SigLIP comparisons.

E3.justification: The two 7B backbones, primary 20-examples-per-label setup, selected-head settings, metrics, dataset reformulations and experimental procedures remain unchanged in Section 4 and the appendices.

E4.justification: Both retain the example/head-count sweeps, classifier/layer/token ablations, transfer analyses, noisy-example robustness, online-learning comparison and qualitative success/failure cases in Sections 4.6-4.7 and Appendices A and C.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 reports five different seeds and means with standard deviations for SAVs and MTV in Table 4b in both versions. No run counts or uncertainty-reporting practices change.

E6.justification: Tables 1-6 and Figures 3-6 retain the same results, curves and qualitative cases. For example, Table 1's LLaVA-OneVision SAVs scores remain 80.8 on MHaluBench, 35.1 on NaturalBench group accuracy and 86.7 on EuroSAT.

T1.justification: The attention, centroid, cosine-similarity, head-scoring and voting formulas in Section 3, together with Algorithm 1's update rules, are unchanged. No assumptions, formal results or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about finetuning-free sparse-head classification, few-shot performance, scaling, interpretability and generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of feature specialization, transfer, noise robustness and weaker online-learning performance are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning internal model access and confidence information for retrieval.

D1.justification: v2 adds a 'Code:' hyperlink at the end of the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation details in Section 4.1 and Appendix B are unchanged. The PDFs establish added access information, without establishing the linked code's availability or completeness.

R1.justification: Section 2's positioning relative to controllable generation, task/function vectors and vision-language embeddings is unchanged. The reference list contains the same cited works.

P1.justification: v2 changes 'SAVs is' to 'SAVs are' in Section 4.7 and corrects 'SAVss' to 'SAVs' in Section 6. Apart from the added code line and updated version/date marking, the prose and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The code addition produces local column and page reflow on pages 1-5, including moving the Section 3 heading from page 3 to page 4. Figures 1-6, Tables 1-7 and Algorithm 1 retain their visual content and structure.

improvement.justification: The added code pointer improves resource-access guidance, and the two wording corrections provide slight editorial polish. These are limited documentation gains: the scientific content and appendices are unchanged, and the PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's availability or quality.
